title: SMIless: Serving DAG-based Inference with Dynamic Invocations under Serverless Computing
problem: ML serving systems on serverless platforms typically optimize resource provisioning and cold start management separately, resulting in higher monetary costs. DAG-based inference workloads require coordinated handling of multiple inference functions with dynamic invocations.
motivation: Reducing deployment costs while maintaining service-level agreements is critical for practical ML inference serving on serverless platforms.
method: SMIless jointly optimizes two decisions usually made separately: resource allocation and cold-start management (minimizing startup delay). For ML workloads with dependent functions organized as chains (DAGs), it pre-warms functions to minimize startup time, adjusting the intensity based on the workload and available hardware. Implemented on OpenFaaS, this approach balances speed against cost.
key_novelty: SMIless jointly optimizes resource allocation and cold-start delay for DAG-based ML inference on serverless platforms through adaptive pre-warming.
contributions: SMIless system that co-optimizes resource configuration and cold-start management for serverless ML inference
Adaptive pre-warming mechanism that balances performance and cost tradeoffs
OpenFaaS-based implementation supporting DAG-based dynamic invocations in heterogeneous environments
Demonstration of 5.73x cost reduction while meeting SLA requirements
primary_theme: Cost-optimized ML serving on serverless platforms
